messages:
maya: Quick note — finished the SmoothQuant + activation-skew experiments for longtrace contexts (64k and 128k). Posting highlights.

nathan: nice! baseline = fp16, right? what hardware?

maya: baseline fp16 on A100-80GB; quant runs on same nodes. configs below.

linh: can you share the metric set? curious about QA EM and model hallucination rate.

maya: we used LM-evals long-ctx QA (sliding-window EM), mean logprob delta, and a simple hallucination proxy (answer len diff > 50 tokens + low confidence). summary:
- FP8 (act-aware mix): +0.4% EM vs fp16 at 64k, +0.2% at 128k.
- AWQ (smoothquant preproc + per-channel scale): -1.8% EM at 64k, -2.5% at 128k.
- GPTQ (w/ layerwise calibration): -0.6% EM at 64k, -1.0% at 128k.
- INT8 symmetric fallback (no act-aware): -3.5% EM / high hallucination bump.

raj: interesting that fp8 beats fp16 on EM for 64k. any idea why?

maya: hypothesis: FP8 act-aware path preserved low-prob tail tokens better under long KV reuse. caching interplay + small activation shift made int-like quantization noisy.

sasha: do you have per-layer activation shift plots?

maya: pasted the rough plot inline (trimmed):
```
Layer 10: +0.02 mean act shift
Layer 25: +0.12 mean act shift
Layer 34: -0.05 mean act shift
Layer 48: +0.28 mean act shift (attention-heavy)
```

nathan: the +0.28 layers correlate with biggest EM drops for AWQ?

maya: yep. AWQ without activation rebalancing loses SNR at those layers when KV length grows. SmoothQuant helps, but AWQ implementation we used requires per-channel scale updates which were brittle at 128k.

linh: config snippet? would love to reproduce.

maya: config we ran:
```
model: redwood-open-13b
context: [65536, 131072]
quant: {
  fp8_actaware: true,
  awq: {
    enabled: true,
    per_channel: true,
    clip_thresh: 3.0
  },
  gptq: { enabled: true, calib_steps: 2048 },
  int8_fallback: { enabled: false }
}
kv_cache: { prefix_cache: true, eviction: adapt }
batching: { dynamic: true }
```

raj: thanks. what about latency/cost tradeoffs? FP8 good but any throughput regressions?

maya: FP8 exec path slightly faster (~8-12% token throughput boost) vs fp16 in our runtime (kernel fusion on A100). AWQ had similar throughput but more variance due to per-channel scaling overhead and occasional re-quantization. GPTQ slower in compile step but runtime comparable to AWQ. INT8 fastest but quality unacceptable for longctx.

deploy-bot: scheduled job 2112233600 -> infra:eng-ml; note: logs uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/2112233445/

sasha: did you run any evals on real chat traces (multi-turn) to see dialog drift?

maya: ran a 2k-dialog trace sim: AWQ shows earlier topic drift by ~1.5 turns at 128k; FP8 and GPTQ kept drift within baseline.

linh: any easy mitigations for AWQ? smoother per-layer clamps or act-split?

maya: tried sigmoid-based clamp + small smoothquant alpha (0.12) — reduced EM drop to -0.9% at 128k (from -2.5%). Runtime cost +3% tokens.

nathan: TL;DR recommendation?

maya: for longtrace production: prefer FP8 act-aware path for now (best EM + modest perf gains). GPTQ is safe fallback for stable latency without heavy per-run calibration. AWQ needs extra smoothing and per-layer clamp tuning before we consider as default on 128k workloads. INT8 only for non-longctx archival use.

raj: can you drop the reproducible run commands and seed?

maya: sure — run script snippet:
```
./runner --model redwood-open-13b --quant fp8_actaware --ctx 131072 --seed 42 --eval long-qa --out /tmp/bench
```

linh: copying to my bucket to run ablations. thanks maya. :thumbsup:

maya: will follow up with full artifacts + point to s3. planning a short doc with per-layer calibration numbers tomorrow.

sasha: great — ping me when doc is up.
